title: Units, Measurement & Problem-Solving
summary: Physics uses SI units and a consistent problem-solving method: list knowns, choose the right equation, check units, and evaluate with sensible significant figures. Unit conversion and order-of-magnitude estimation keep answers grounded.

SI units.in_class: meter, kilogram, second, and derived N, J, W.

unit conversion.plain: Rewriting a value in other units.
unit conversion.in_class: Multiply by ratios equal to 1 so units cancel.

significant figures.plain: The reliable digits of a measurement.
significant figures.in_class: The result can't be more precise than its inputs.

dimensional analysis.in_class: Both sides must share the same units.

order of magnitude.in_class: For fast estimates and reality checks.

scientific notation.in_class: Handles very large or small values.

problem-solving strategy.plain: A systematic approach to physics problems.

concept_sections.heading: SI units
concept_sections.explanation: Mechanical quantities build from meter, kilogram, and second; derived units like the newton ($\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}^2$) and joule ($\mathrm{N\cdot m}$) combine them.

concept_sections.heading: Unit conversion
concept_sections.explanation: Convert by multiplying by ratios equal to 1, arranged so unwanted units cancel and the target unit remains.

concept_sections.heading: Significant figures
concept_sections.explanation: Report only the digits your data support: multiplication/division keeps the fewest significant figures, addition keeps the fewest decimal places.
math_steps: Count sig figs in each input.

concept_sections.heading: Dimensional checks
concept_sections.explanation: A correct equation is dimensionally consistent — every term has the same units. A mismatch signals an error before you even plug in numbers.
math_steps: List the units of each term.
Fix the equation if they don't.

concept_sections.heading: Estimation and strategy
concept_sections.explanation: Approach every problem the same way: identify knowns and the unknown, pick an equation, solve symbolically, then evaluate — and use order-of-magnitude estimates to sanity-check.
